subject: Stackline connector: webhook 502s — fallback & escalation plan
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@stackline.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Marketplace Ops <marketplace-ops@stackline.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Stackline connector: repeated webhook 502s — escalation + fallback plan?

Hi Jonas,

We started seeing a spike of 502 responses from the Redwood connector that takes our marketplace order events and enriches them with inventory metadata. Impact: ~12% of enrichment calls are failing during peak (08:45-09:30 PDT) which led to delayed publish for affected SKUs.

Attached a short incident-log-snippet and the webhook headers showing retry behavior. We’ve already bumped retries on our side but failures persist. Can we do the following immediately?
- Route affected requests to a lower-memory model variant (canary) while your infra investigates
- Add a short-term retry/backoff tweak on the Redwood side (3→5 attempts with jitter)
- Stand up a quick bridge for triage if we can’t stabilize in 30–45m

This is affecting a small set of marketplace sellers but the downstream order processing SLA is slipping. Please advise who from Redwood ops is on-call and what your escalation path is — we’ll open an incident on our side too.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Integrations, Stackline Systems
Attachments: incident-log-snippet.txt, webhook-headers.json
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@stackline.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stackline connector: repeated webhook 502s — escalation + fallback plan?

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. Sorry you’re seeing this. I’ve looped in Sergio (runtime) and Camila (partnership engineering) and Marissa from our commercial team so we can coordinate both the technical mitigation and any contract implications.

Immediate actions we’ll take now (I’ll own the coordination):
1) I’ve asked Sergio to enable a temporary routing rule to the `redwood-lite-quant` variant for Stackline traffic for the affected route. That should drop memory pressure and reduce transient 502s.
2) We’ll increase server-side retries to 5 with randomized backoff for that route for the next 2 hours.
3) We’ll spin up a 30-minute bridge at 09:40 PDT (dial-in to follow) and share a mutual action plan doc for sign-off.

I attached a draft MAP (MAP-draft-Stackline.docx) with proposed responsibilities and SLAs for the mitigation window. Please review quickly and let me know if the proposed times and actions work.

If this isn’t stable within the bridge window we’ll escalate to a full incident via SUP-7842 and run the rollback/fallback in the runbook.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Partner Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Elena Rossi <elena@stackline.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stackline connector: repeated webhook 502s — escalation + fallback plan?

Elena, Jonas — quick technical notes from runtime:

What I see from the logs you sent: rapid connection resets at the gateway layer, plus occasional KV cache thrashing when sequence lengths spike. The most reliable mitigation with the least customer impact is:
- Route Stackline → `redwood-lite-quant` (lower mem, fewer parallel KV shards) — this is a hot patch and reversible.
- Adjust server-side keepalive and connection timeout to 10s for that route (reduces mid-request disconnects seen in the logs).
- Add an exponential backoff on retries (base 500ms, multiplier 2, cap 6s) and jitter.

Runbook excerpt (attached runbook_snippet.md): if 502 rate > 5% sustained for 15 minutes after routing, elevate to severity P1, open SUP-7842, and trigger capacity-boost (add one dedicated shard for the route).

I’ll push the routing change now and report back in 5–7 minutes. If Stackline can tighten the client-side timeout to 12s and increase jitter on their retry loop that will make things much less bursty.

—Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: runbook_snippet.md
From: Elena Rossi <elena@stackline.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Marketplace Ops <marketplace-ops@stackline.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stackline connector: repeated webhook 502s — fallback & escalation plan

Thanks Sergio — we can change our timeout/jitter on the publisher within the hour. We’re also able to flip to an internal queuing layer for the most critical sellers as a stop-gap.

A couple of commercial items to surface while we coordinate: if this incident exceeds 4 hours of customer-visible degradation, Stackline will request a credit (per section 6.2 of RDW-ENT-2025-714). Can you confirm Redwood’s willingness to review the credit if the mitigation window extends? Also, please confirm you’ve assigned an incident number we can reference.

We’ll be on the 09:40 bridge. Dial-in?

—Elena
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@stackline.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stackline connector: fallback & escalation plan — commercial note

Elena — thanks for flagging the contract clause. I’ll own the commercial follow-up. For transparency: we’ll start capturing the affected request counts and error minutes during the mitigation window (Jonas/Sergio can supply tokenized metrics). If the incident meets the credit threshold in section 6.2 we’ll draft a credit brief and submit it to Finance within 48 hours.

For now, let’s keep the bridge focused on stabilization. I’ll join and collect the metrics we need to correlate impact to the contract.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Partnerships — Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@stackline.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stackline connector: webhook 502s — post-incident plan and next steps

Team — quick post-status update after the bridge and follow-up:
- Routing to `redwood-lite-quant` reduced 502s from 12% → 1.6% during peak; we left the rule active until 14:30 PDT and then reverted when KV load normalized.
- Server-side retries/backoff added for the protected route during the mitigation window.
- Stackline patched publisher timeouts/jitter per Sergio’s recommendation; their queuing stop-gap is in place for the critical sellers.
- Incident recorded under SUP-7842; I added the MAP link for signatures.

Action items:
1) Elena/Stackline: confirm acceptance of the MAP and sign the doc (link in related_links).
2) Sergio: follow up with a short runbook PR to make the route-timeout tweak a documented emergency lever.
3) Marissa: prepare the credit brief only if our metrics show >4 hours of customer-visible degradation (capture window: 05/28 08:30–12:30 PDT).
4) Camila: schedule a 1:1 onboarding review to tighten producer backpressure patterns (proactive work).

Thanks everyone for the rapid turnaround — Jon as owner, I’ll keep the ticket open for 72 hours for monitoring.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Partner Ops, Redwood Inference
